changes.why: CR-PBI001-01: new verifier_outcome() reads the lane ver outcome through VERIFIER_TIERS: an outcome label (JSON outcome key or Outcome:), then a Verdict-labelled, bold or code word, then a bare word. Case-insensitive; a word after a negation (NEGATED) is skipped; fallback-declared wins when a tier holds both words. verdict_of() tries it first on lane ver only; the verifier words leave TOKEN, so other lanes read as before and ver still falls back to the review tokens. CR-PBI001-04: when a session parse raises and its cached result is reused, the export gets a copy whose rows pass through carried(); the cache entry (signature and rows) is left as read, so the session is re-read next run

CR-PBI001-02: RUN_ID copies local/records.py _SEGMENT (fullmatch; non-empty, no / or \, no C0/C1 control characters, not . or ..); manual() raises the same named ValueError (row index, id, field) for an id outside it

CR-PBI001-03: later_items() keeps a nested item (list line indented 4+ spaces or a tab) and its continuation lines in its idea's description as joined text, marker included, instead of dropping them; the nested flag is removed

runs-table lane list gains other (review follow-up) and states how a verifier's word is read; backlog later text documents nested items kept in the description; refresh step 1 documents the manual id form and the session-level running-row carry
failing-first tests for the verifier outcome (fallback headline + not exercised, JSON outcome block, any case, negations, bare preference) and the session-level carry
failing-first tests for unsafe manual ids, dotted ids that stay valid, a drift guard reading local/records.py as data via ast, and nested Later items kept in the description

follow_ups.note: Re-review the working-tree diff in the PBI-001 worktree for round 2 (CR-PBI001-01..04).

RUN_ID matches local _SEGMENT exactly, so an id such as .x is accepted by both forms, yet it writes out/runs/.x.json, which refresh.py's dotfile-skipping glob never pushes. Tightening it would diverge from the local form; decide in both places together (local/** is outside this PBI's areas).

NEGATED covers not, never, no, cannot, without and n't, optionally followed by be/been/being/yet/fully/actually/really. Phrasings such as 'unable to be exercised' or 'skipped rather than exercised' are not caught and read as a bare exercised (still beaten by any bare or labelled fallback-declared); widen the list only if real verifier transcripts show them.
Reviewer follow-up stands: the PBI rule (up to 3 leading spaces is a new idea) differs from CommonMark's parent-content-column rule; update the spec rule, not the code.
